content: 1. Midwifery continuity of care is recommended as a context-specific intervention to improve postnatal care delivery. This approach ensures that women receive consistent and personalized care throughout their pregnancy, childbirth, and postnatal period. 2. Task-sharing components of postnatal care delivery are recommended. This involves redistributing specific tasks among healthcare providers to optimize the use of available resources and improve access to essential maternal and newborn health services. 3. Recruitment and retention of healthcare staff in rural and remote areas are critical. Policymakers should implement a comprehensive package of interventions, including education, regulation, incentives, and personal and professional support, to strengthen the health workforce in these underserved regions. 4. The involvement of men in postnatal care and maternal and newborn health is recommended. Interventions should encourage men’s participation during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period to support women’s self-care, improve home care practices, and promote the use of skilled care for both women and newborns. These interventions must respect women’s autonomy and decision-making while supporting their care for themselves and their newborns. 5. Home-based records are recommended as a tool to improve the continuity and quality of care for women and newborns. These records facilitate communication between healthcare providers and families, ensuring that essential health information is accessible and utilized effectively. 6. Digital targeted client communication is recommended in specific contexts. This includes using digital platforms to provide tailored health information and reminders to women and families, enhancing their engagement with postnatal care services. 7. Digital birth notifications are recommended in settings where they provide individual-level data to the health system or civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) systems. These systems must have the capacity to respond to the notifications effectively. 8. The WHO postnatal care model emphasizes the importance of a minimum of four postnatal care contacts, with a particular focus on the first two weeks after birth. This period is critical for promoting health, identifying potential problems, and supporting the transition to well-woman and well-infant care. 9. The guideline highlights the importance of postnatal care during the first 24 hours after birth, regardless of the place of birth. A minimum 24-hour stay in a health facility with continuous care and monitoring is recommended to address potential complications and prepare for the transition to home care. 10. At least three additional postnatal care contacts should occur during the first six weeks after birth. These contacts should include effective clinical practices, timely information, and psychosocial and emotional support provided by skilled and compassionate health workers. 11. An effective referral system is essential for postnatal care. This includes communication between facilityand community-based care providers and coordination with transport workers to address complications promptly. 12. Monitoring and evaluation of the implementation and impact of these recommendations are crucial. Clear criteria and indicators should be established to assess progress at the health service, sub-national, and national levels. 13. The WHO guideline consolidates current recommendations for effective and safe clinical and non-clinical interventions during the postnatal period. It aims to improve the quality of care for women and newborns, focusing on a positive postnatal experience. 14. A positive postnatal experience is defined as one where women, newborns, and families receive consistent information and reassurance from motivated health workers. Their needs are recognized within a well-resourced and culturally respectful health system. 15. The guideline is intended for national and sub-national public health policymakers, program managers, health facility managers, healthcare workers, non-governmental organizations, professional societies, academic staff, and women and parents’ groups. 16. The scope of the guideline includes the care of all women and adolescent girls in the postpartum period and newborns in any health facility or community-based setting. It focuses on the essential postnatal care package that all women and newborns should receive. 17. The guideline complements existing WHO guidance on immediate care after birth, management of complications during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period, and care for preterm and low birthweight infants. 18. The recommendations emphasize the importance of quality, respectful, and individualized care throughout the pregnancy-to-postnatal continuum, in line with a human rights-based approach. 19. The guideline updates and expands upon the 2014 WHO recommendations on postnatal care and integrates new evidence to improve the quality of care for women and newborns. 20. The priority questions and outcomes guiding the evidence synthesis for this guideline focus on essential care during the postnatal period, including maternal and newborn assessments, interventions for common symptoms, preventive measures, mental health support, contraception, nutrition, breastfeeding, and health promotion. 21. The guideline recognizes the diverse needs of women and newborns, including those with additional health and social needs, and emphasizes the importance of providing high-quality care to all individuals, regardless of their circumstances.
